payload.body_markdown:
Owner instruction, recorded rather than acted on: **Kosmos-Oden is to be submitted to `obsidianmd/obsidian-releases`**, the Obsidian community plugin registry. Noted only. No scope agreed, nothing prepared, nothing submitted. It is logged here because it would be the first time this programme publishes a Kosmos artifact to a third-party registry, and because a registry submission freezes exactly the identifiers that changed today.

No action requested.

## Three merges landed on Kosmos-Oden `main` today

| PR | squash | what |
|---|---|---|
| #42 | `5d56d5d` | Release 0.8.2; Engine library pin moved to `650eab4a6752227cae336d7556a57826c22a0d5a` |
| #43 | `e1705fa` | Kosmos-Oden branding restored; WebDAV secret migration; sync-exclusion fix |
| #44 | `a38aefe` | Renderer overview pixel-ratio ceiling and capture pin restored |

#29 closed as superseded by #43. All three were merged with owner admin bypass of the review requirement; every CI check passed on its own, so the bypass covered the missing review only.

**The pin is the part that reaches outside this project.** Kosmos `main` previously depended on Engine `41172b9`, which is not an ancestor of Engine `main` and does not descend from `v2.1.2`. It now depends on `650eab4`, which is on Engine `main` and descends from the tag. Any statement written against the old pin was describing an off-main dependency.

## Identifiers renamed, and the ones deliberately left alone

Renamed in #43: `VIEW_TYPE` `vault-kosmos-view` to `kosmos-oden-view`; `KOSMOS_PROTOCOL` `vault-kosmos` to `kosmos-oden`; root CSS class `.vault-kosmos-root` to `.kosmos-oden-root`; command id `open-vault-kosmos` to `open-kosmos-oden`; `BUILD-INFO.json` `project` to `kosmos-oden`; manifest `name` `Vault Kosmos (KRS)` to `Kosmos-Oden`. Nomenclature followed through the docs, including `KRS` to `Kosmos-Oden` and `KRS-Lite` to `Kosmos-Oden Lite`.

Not renamed, on purpose: upstream MIT attribution to `H4R7W16/vault-kosmos`, a real external repository, and changelog entries under `[0.6.5-beta.2]` documenting a path that genuinely was `vault-kosmos` before the 0.6.6 plugin-id rename. A blanket sweep rewrote both and it had to be reverted.

Two identifiers name already-persisted user data and are held for compatibility: the previous view type stays registered so a saved workspace keeps its pane, and the pre-rename Nextcloud secret key is still read and promoted on first access. The per-vault hash derives from plugin id and vault name, neither of which changed.

## One lesson worth carrying to any parity work

The brand sweep flattened both compatibility literals into their new values, turning the view-type alias and the credential migration into silent no-ops. `npm run verify` passed anyway: 291 tests, none covering them. It was caught only by grepping the built bundle for the legacy strings.

**A rename sweep destroys backward-compatibility constants, and a green suite is not evidence they survived.** Assert legacy identifiers at the artifact level, not the source level. `scripts/check-artifacts.mjs` now does exactly that for both, confirmed to fail when either is removed, and both sites carry a do-not-rebrand comment.

Related trap for anyone inspecting a Kosmos bundle: the renderer is base64-embedded inside `main.js` and decoded at runtime, and the bundle is minified, so grepping `main.js` for renderer identifiers always returns zero and looks like a failed build. Check `kosmos-oden-stand-alone.html` instead, or decode the longest base64 string literal out of `main.js`.

## Standing on the registry item

Not started. Two questions already visible, neither investigated and neither claimed to be a blocker: the version-suffixed install folder convention (`kosmos-oden_v0.8.2`) against a registry that keys on the plugin id, and `docs/COMMUNITY-PLUGIN.md`, which already exists and should be reconciled rather than replaced.
